title: The Scintillating World of Interest Rates
summary: Josh and Chuck explain interest rates, starting with the basics of borrowing and lending and the risk premium behind interest. They cover nominal versus real interest rates, the Federal Reserve (created 1913, twelve regional banks and a seven-member board), bank panics such as Louis Remy's ride to Portland, reserve requirements, the federal funds rate and discount rate, and how Fed open-market buying and selling of Treasury securities influences bank lending, stocks, and the dollar. They discuss inflation (the Fed's roughly two percent target), demand-pull versus cost-push inflation, stagflation, the Fed's recent half-point rate hike, the risk of recession, and the soft-landing goal. The episode closes with a listener mail about a gin and tonic recipe with orange, rosemary and black pepper, and a note about the studio move.

segments.title: Studio farewell and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck note this is one of the last recordings in their studio before a move, reminisce about the space, and set up the episode on interest rates after the Fed's recent half-point hike.

segments.title: Interest rate basics and the Fed's recent hike
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Fed's half-point rate increase as an attempt to cool inflation and create a soft landing. They describe interest as the price of lending and compensation for risk, and contrast secured debt like mortgages with unsecured credit card debt.

segments.title: Nominal versus real interest rates and mortgage pricing
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss why longer loans carry higher rates, why 15-year mortgages are cheaper, and how inflation erodes repayment value, distinguishing the nominal rate from the real rate. They also describe how banks forecast inflation when setting mortgage rates.

segments.title: Chain effects of mortgage rates and the Federal Reserve's founding
segments.summary: The hosts trace how rising mortgage rates ripple into housing, construction, and foreclosures. They then give an overview of the Federal Reserve, created in 1913 with twelve regional banks and a seven-member board, to stabilize a banking system marked by bank runs.

segments.title: Bank panics and the Louis Remy story
segments.summary: Josh tells the story of Louis Remy, who rode from Sacramento to Portland after his bank failed, to recover his savings. The hosts discuss how bank panics spread as a chain reaction.

segments.title: Reserve requirements, federal funds rate, and discount rate
segments.summary: The hosts explain that banks must hold reserves at the Fed, averaged over two weeks. Banks borrow overnight from each other at the federal funds rate, or from the Fed at the higher discount rate, which has primary, secondary, and seasonal tiers.

segments.title: Movie tangent
segments.summary: The hosts digress into recent films, including The Green Night and David Lowery, and discuss Raising Arizona and other movies.

segments.title: How the Fed moves rates through Treasury securities and the dollar
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Fed sets a target for the federal funds rate and nudges it through buying and selling Treasury bills with primary dealers. They describe how this affects bank lending, stock market attractiveness, and the value of the dollar.

segments.title: Inflation, demand-pull versus cost-push, and recession risk
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Fed's roughly two percent inflation target, stagflation, and demand-pull and cost-push theories. They examine the balancing act of cooling prices without causing recession and offer tips for preparing for a downturn.

segments.title: Listener mail: orange rosemary gin and tonic
segments.summary: A listener named Meg from Australia shares a gin and tonic recipe with orange, rosemary, and cracked black pepper, and the hosts react.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck invite listeners to send emails and close the show.
